tagline.text: A hilltop mall above Burnham Park, among the largest shopping centers in northern Luzon

location.label: Location
location.text: Luneta Hill, Upper Session Road, Baguio City

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (indoor mall; the cool, clear months of November–May are best for getting around)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–2,500 (per person, covering a meal, transport, light shopping and one or two rides)

airport.label: Nearest airport

children.text: SM City Baguio opened on November 21, 2003 on Luneta Hill at the top of Session Road, and it is one of the biggest malls in northern Luzon. Its open-air design suited to the Cordillera highlands, its rooftop views and the neighboring Sky Ranch amusement park make it useful for shopping, rainy-day plans and family outings alike.

SM City Baguio is a large shopping mall on Luneta Hill, the hilltop where Session Road ends in central Baguio. Its address on the official SM page is Luneta Hill, Upper Session Road, and it stands across from Baguio City Hall, looking down toward Burnham Park. It is run by SM Prime Holdings and, according to Wikipedia, opened on November 21, 2003. The site was once the Pines Hotel, which burned down in 1984, and SM reportedly won the lot at a government development bank auction in 1988. Even today people in Baguio still talk about a big mall rising on a pine-covered hill, so it is both a symbol of the city and a subject of debate.

The building is a little different from other SM malls. Wikipedia describes it as one of the first SM Supermalls built without air conditioning in its common areas, and says it drew inspiration from Cordillera design. That works because Baguio sits about 1,500 meters above sea level and stays cool all year. Air moves through an open central space, and there is a veranda modeled on the Banaue Rice Terraces. The main mall has several floors, and beside it are the North Terraces and Sunset Terraces, which opened in stages in 2019–2020, plus a parking annex. Floor-area figures differ by source: the official SM page gives roughly 100,000 square meters, while Wikipedia gives a larger number. It is enough to know that it is one of the largest malls in northern Luzon.

For travelers this mall is less an attraction than a base for your Baguio plans. You can handle currency exchange, a SIM card, a pharmacy, grocery shopping, a movie and a meal in one place, and according to Wikipedia a Department of Foreign Affairs consular office is also inside. Baguio can be cloudy or rainy even from December to February, and June to October brings frequent rainy-season showers, so the mall is especially handy when a plan for Burnham Park or an outdoor viewpoint falls through. You can walk up Session Road to reach it, so it is easy to combine with the central sights in a one-day itinerary.

There is also some background worth knowing. In 2012, more than 5,000 residents protested on Session Road over plans to cut about 100 pine trees on Luneta Hill for the mall's expansion, and after court battles the Supreme Court permanently banned cutting or earth-balling trees on Luneta Hill in April 2019, according to Wikipedia. That is why locals may tell you the pine trees you see around the mall were saved by citizens. Even if you only come to browse the shops, knowing this changes how you see the city.

Luneta Hill sits at the top of Session Road, so Burnham Park and the downtown area spread out in front of you. Many visitors watch the city lights come on at dusk from the upper terrace and viewing areas. It faces City Hall, so it is easy to find.

blocks.title: An open layout where cool air flows through

children.text: Because the common areas use little air conditioning, outside air circulates even at midday, and you avoid the heavy chill of Manila malls. Rain can blow into some areas but not others, so bring an umbrella. It is a shopping mall experience that suits a mountain city.

This amusement park is on Rambakan Drive next to the mall. According to Wikipedia it opened on November 8, 2018 and has rides such as the Baguio Eye Ferris wheel, a Viking ship and a drop tower. As of November 2026 two sources put a single Baguio Eye ride at ₱180, ordinary rides at about ₱60–120 (the Road Train is ₱80), and a separate cash entrance fee is reportedly about ₱50 Monday to Thursday and ₱80 Friday to Sunday and holidays. The official SM listing gives park hours of
, and prices can change, so confirm on site.

At SM Store you can buy clothes and household goods in one stop, and the SM Supermarket on the lower level carries gift foods such as Baguio strawberry jam, peanut brittle, ube jam and coffee. Korean instant noodles and seasonings are not hard to find either, so long-stay visitors often do their first grocery run here.

According to Wikipedia, the third level has four cinemas and the Cyberzone electronics area. Check showtimes and prices in the SM Cinema app. It is a good way to spend two or three hours on a rainy afternoon.

blocks.title: A wide choice of places to eat

children.text: There are food courts, fast-food chains, cafes and Filipino restaurants on every level. Baguio is known for coffee, strawberries and highland vegetables, and some shops feature them. Lines get long at weekend lunch and dinner, so it helps to go a little early.

Wikipedia says this is the only SM Supermall that opens all year, including Holy Week. In the Philippines most shops and restaurants close during Holy Week, so when visitors flood Baguio, this is a place where you can worry less about meals and groceries. Check the official SM announcement for that week's hours.

According to Wikipedia, a DFA consular office on the upper basement level handles passport business for residents of northern Luzon. Most travelers will not need it, but long-stay visitors with a passport problem should know about it. Check DFA announcements for booking methods and whether it is operating.

items.subtitle: Shopping, meals and a movie indoors

children.text: Arrive when the mall opens at
and scan the floor directory to see where things are. It is a quiet time to look around.
At the SM Supermarket on the lower level, pick up Baguio gifts such as strawberry jam, peanut brittle and coffee, and take care of currency exchange and a SIM card at this time too.
Eat lunch at the food court or a cafe. On weekends, I recommend hurrying in around
Browse the Cyberzone and the clothing stores, then step out onto an open terrace to see the city after the rain.
Finish with a movie or a rest at a cafe.
Because the mall is on a mountain, the temperature drops after sunset, so bring a light jacket.

items.title: Fitting it into a day in the city
items.subtitle: A route from Session Road up to the mall

children.text: Start with central sights such as Burnham Park and Baguio Cathedral.
Walk up Session Road, looking at the shops and street food. It is uphill, so take your time.
Arrive at SM City Baguio for lunch and a rest.
If you are with family, ride the Baguio Eye at Sky Ranch.
At dusk, look over the city from a viewing area, then go back to your hotel by taxi or on foot.
Session Road is a pleasant street to walk, but the way down is easy while the way up leaves you short of breath.
From Manila (Cubao, Pasay, Sampaloc and elsewhere), take a long-distance bus such as Victory Liner to Baguio. Guides say a day bus takes about
6–7 hours
and a night bus about
5–6 hours
According to August to November 2026 guides, a Victory Liner regular air-conditioned fare is
depending on the terminal, and Deluxe and higher classes run
. Fuel surcharges may add to this, so check Victory Liner's latest announcements for schedules and fares.
Guides say Victory Liner's Baguio terminal is within walking distance of the mall, but sources differ on its exact location (Governor Pack Road or Utility Road), so confirm locally.
Tickets sell out quickly on weekends and holiday periods, so book ahead.
Taxis can take you to the mall easily from anywhere in the city. Check the meter fare or use a ride-hailing app such as Grab.
Jeepneys run fixed routes, so ask the driver where it is going before you board. Guides put short-distance fares at about
. The 2026 national increase sets traditional jeepneys at ₱14 for the first 4 km and modern ones at ₱17, but guides disagree on when it applies in Baguio, so confirm locally.
You can walk up to the mall from Burnham Park and Session Road. Tricycles reportedly are not allowed on major roads such as Session Road and Governor Pack Road.

It is an indoor mall, so you can go at any time of year, and it is actually a good place to be on a rainy or cloudy day. From November to May the weather is cool and clear, which makes the upper terrace and Sky Ranch more enjoyable and makes it easy to link with a city itinerary.

The mall and nearby roads get crowded on weekends and holidays, in the December Christmas season, during the Panagbenga Flower Festival in February and during Holy Week. Weekday mornings are the quietest, and during Holy Week crowds gather here because it stays open while other places close.

Hotels and guesthouses cluster around Session Road and Burnham Park, within walking distance of the mall, which is convenient if you plan to use it often. The downtown roads are narrow, though, and on weekend evenings walking is often faster than a car. Hotel rates rise during Christmas and Panagbenga season, so book early.

For meals, you can keep it simple at the food court and chain restaurants inside, and in the evening it is worth heading down to local restaurants on Session Road or toward the market. Baguio is famous for strawberries, highland vegetables and coffee, so many people buy food gifts at the supermarket. Tenants change often, so check the on-site directories or the official SM app.
Bags are checked at every entrance, so leave large luggage and sharp objects at your hotel.
The official SM listing gives regular hours of about
, extended to
on Saturdays. Hours change around holidays and year-end, so check the latest announcements.
When you take a taxi, saying SM Baguio or Luneta Hill gets you there.
There are slippery slopes on rainy days, so wear low, non-slip shoes.
Baguio gets chilly after dark, so bring a light jacket.
Sky Ranch prices vary with the date and promotions, so check on site or in official announcements.
Even though the bus terminal is close to the mall, take a taxi rather than walking if you have luggage. There are many uphill stretches.
Use the parking annex. It fills up easily on weekends, so public transport is recommended.
Roads around the mall are extremely congested on weekends, during Holy Week and in the Christmas season. Allow plenty of time.
Pickpockets work in crowded malls and on Session Road, so carry your bag in front and keep your wallet and phone deep in your pockets.
Because of the open layout with little air conditioning, areas where rain blows in have slippery floors.
Rides at Sky Ranch have height and age limits, so check on site.
Compare rates at the money changers inside the mall, and do not exchange a large amount at just one place.
Bus and jeepney fares and schedules change often, so check the latest announcements.
Walk down about
10 minutes
from the mall and you reach Baguio's main street, lined with shops and restaurants.
A large park in the heart of the city below the mall, known for its lake and bicycle rentals. You can get there on foot.
A pinkish church at the upper end of Session Road, within walking distance.
A former US military rest-and-recreation base with pine forests and walking trails. Take a taxi.
